name: n09-relay
title: DHCP relay agent
spec: Left to right: Client in a rack VLAN, a router/switch box labelled 'DHCP relay agent', a central DHCP server. Arrow 1 client to relay: 'DHCP broadcast (does not cross routers)'. Arrow 2 relay to server: 'unicast, relay adds its interface address in giaddr'. Arrow 3 server to client path back: 'server reads giaddr to pick the scope (subnet pool)'. Orange highlight on giaddr. Small options chip: 'option 3 router, 6 DNS, 51 lease time, 66/67 TFTP server and boot file (PXE)'. Monospace for giaddr and option numbers.
cap: A relay agent turns a local broadcast into a unicast to a central server and tags it with giaddr so the server picks the right scope.

name: n09-pxe
title: PXE boot of a bare-metal GPU node
spec: Four numbered steps left to right with arrows. 1 'NIC firmware (PXE ROM or UEFI HTTP boot): DHCP DISCOVER, vendor class PXEClient, option 93 architecture'. 2 'DHCP server replies: address + next-server (TFTP) + filename (for example ipxe.efi)'. 3 'firmware downloads bootloader iPXE; script over HTTP fetches kernel, initrd, kickstart/autoinstall/cloud-init seed'. 4 'OS installer or provisioner (BCM, MAAS, Ironic) configures the node; then node's own DHCP client runs'. Orange note under step 1-2: 'Only one DHCP server may answer a subnet'. Monospace for PXEClient, ipxe.efi.
anchor: ### PXE boot of bare-metal GPU nodes
cap: A bare-metal node gets its address, bootloader, kernel and installer one step at a time over DHCP, TFTP and HTTP.

name: n09-snatdnat
title: SNAT versus DNAT
spec: Two horizontal flows. Top row 'SNAT / PAT (outbound)': private host -> NAT box -> Internet; the NAT box rewrites the SOURCE address (and translated source port for PAT); use: egress to the Internet, MASQUERADE, Cloud NAT. Bottom row 'DNAT (inbound)': client from Internet -> NAT box -> inside server; the NAT box rewrites the DESTINATION; use: port forwarding, Kubernetes Services, Docker -p. Small chip for static NAT (1:1) fixed inside address to fixed outside address, elastic IPs. Orange highlight on 'NAT is not a firewall'. Green bar: 'If you see MASQUERADE in a rule, you are looking at PAT'.
cap: SNAT rewrites the source on the way out and DNAT rewrites the destination on the way in.
